claim: Lhx3 and Tgfb1i1 were identified as DF4-binding proteins in R28 rat retinal precursor cells through proteomic screening.
source: In a proteomic screen for DF4-binding proteins in R28 rat RPCs, we identified Lhx3 (LIM domain homeobox 3) and Hic-5 (hydrogen peroxide induced clone 5)/Tgfb1i1 (tumor growth factor-β1 induced transcript one protein)/Ara55 (androgen receptor-associated protein 55) as potential candidates (Figure 1B; see Materials and methods for details).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from a proteomic screen shown in Figure 1B and described in the Materials and methods section.

claim: Lhx3 and Tgfb1i1 share the LIM protein-protein interaction domain.
source: These proteins share the LIM (LIN-11, Isl1, or MEC-3) protein-protein interaction domain (Karlsson et al., 1990; Way and Chalfie, 1988).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous literature (Karlsson et al., 1990; Way and Chalfie, 1988) establishing the LIM domain as a protein-protein interaction domain.

claim: Lhx3 contains a homeodomain and acts as a transcription factor.
source: In addition, Lhx3 contains a homeodomain and acts as a transcription factor (Bridwell et al., 2001; Roberson et al., 1994).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Bridwell et al., 2001; Roberson et al., 1994) that characterized Lhx3 as a transcription factor.

claim: Tgfb1i1 has four leucine-rich domains (LDs) that mediate interactions with other LD-containing proteins.
source: Tgfb1i1 has four leucine-rich domains (LDs), which mediate interactions with other LD-containing protein, and four LIM domains, which mediate both self-oligomerization and interactions with other LIM domain-containing proteins (Mori et al., 2006; Nishiya et al., 1999).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Mori et al., 2006; Nishiya et al., 1999) that characterized the domain structure and function of Tgfb1i1.

claim: Tgfb1i1 has four LIM domains that mediate both self-oligomerization and interactions with other LIM domain-containing proteins.
source: Tgfb1i1 has four leucine-rich domains (LDs), which mediate interactions with other LD-containing protein, and four LIM domains, which mediate both self-oligomerization and interactions with other LIM domain-containing proteins (Mori et al., 2006; Nishiya et al., 1999).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Mori et al., 2006; Nishiya et al., 1999) that characterized the domain structure and function of Tgfb1i1.

claim: Lhx3 is absent from the embryonic mouse retina.
source: Lhx3 is absent from the embryonic mouse retina, but is expressed in bipolar cells beginning around the first post-natal week (Figure 1C, top; Figure 1—figure supplement 1A) (Balasubramanian et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A, and corroborated by citation to Balasubramanian et al., 2014.

claim: Lhx3 is expressed in bipolar cells beginning around the first post-natal week.
source: Lhx3 is absent from the embryonic mouse retina, but is expressed in bipolar cells beginning around the first post-natal week (Figure 1C, top; Figure 1—figure supplement 1A) (Balasubramanian et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A, and corroborated by citation to Balasubramanian et al., 2014.

claim: Tgfb1i1 is expressed in most of post-natal retina.
source: Tgfb1i1 is expressed in most of post-natal retina, but is absent from the embryonic and adult mouse retinas (Figure 1C, bottom; Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Tgfb1i1 is absent from the embryonic and adult mouse retinas.
source: Tgfb1i1 is expressed in most of post-natal retina, but is absent from the embryonic and adult mouse retinas (Figure 1C, bottom; Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Lhx3- and Tgfb1i1-expressing cells in P8 retinas show no Pax6 α-enhancer activity.
source: We also noticed Lhx3- and Tgfb1i1-expressing cells in P8 retinas show no Pax6 α-enhancer activity (Figure 1C), as visualized by an GFP reporter in Pax6 α-enhancer::Cre-IRES-GFP (P6α-CreiGFP) mice (Marquardt et al., 2001).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 1C using a GFP reporter mouse line, with citation to Marquardt et al., 2001 for the reporter line.

claim: There is a potential negative relationship between Lhx3 and Tgfb1i1 and the Pax6 α-enhancer activity.
source: This suggests a potential negative relationship between these LIM domain proteins and the α-enhancer activity.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the observation that Lhx3- and Tgfb1i1-expressing cells show no Pax6 α-enhancer activity.

claim: Lhx3 and Tgfb1i1 in P7 retinal nuclear extracts bind wild-type DF4 dsDNA (DF4-WT) but not mutant DF4 dsDNA (DF4-MUT).
source: To validate our screening results, we further examined the binding of those LIM-domain containing proteins in P7 retinal nuclear extracts to DF4 sequence, and found Lhx3 and Tgfb1i1 in these extracts bind wild-type DF4 dsDNA (DF4-WT) but not mutant DF4 dsDNA (DF4-MUT) in which the 5'-ATTA-3' homeodomain target sequence is replaced with 5'-CGGC-3' (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A demonstrating differential binding to wild-type versus mutant DF4 sequences.

claim: In vitro-translated Lhx3 specifically binds the DF4 oligomer.
source: Not only the endogenous Lhx3 but also in vitro-translated Lhx3 specifically binds the DF4 oligomer (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by EMSA data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2B demonstrating direct binding of in vitro-translated Lhx3 to DF4.

claim: In vitro-translated Tgfb1i1 does not bind the DF4 oligomer.
source: In vitro-translated Tgfb1i1, however, lacks a DNA-binding motif, and so does not bind the DF4 oligomer (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by EMSA data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2B and by the knowledge that Tgfb1i1 lacks a DNA-binding motif.

claim: Tgfb1i1 binds the α-enhancer indirectly, possibly via an interaction with another DF4-binding protein like Lhx3.
source: This suggests Tgfb1i1 binds the α-enhancer indirectly, possibly via an interaction with another DF4-binding protein like Lhx3.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the observation that Tgfb1i1 lacks DNA-binding motifs but is found in complexes with DF4 DNA.

claim: In the mouse retina, Lhx3 and Tgfb1i1 interact specifically with the α-enhancer but not the ectodermal enhancer.
source: We found that, in the mouse retina, Lhx3 and Tgfb1i1 interact specifically with the α-enhancer but not the ectodermal enhancer (Figure 1D,E).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP data shown in Figure 1D and 1E demonstrating specific enrichment at the α-enhancer.

claim: Lhx2 shows specific binding to the DF4 sequence.
source: We found Lhx2, but not Isl1, shows specific binding to the DF4 sequence (Figure 1—figure supplement 3C).
evidence: The claim is supported by EMSA data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3C.

claim: Isl1 does not show specific binding to the DF4 sequence.
source: We found Lhx2, but not Isl1, shows specific binding to the DF4 sequence (Figure 1—figure supplement 3C).
evidence: The claim is supported by EMSA data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3C.

claim: Isl1 binds DF3, which contains the predicted Isl1 binding sequence 5'-CATTAG-3'.
source: Isl1 instead binds DF3, which contains the predicted Isl1 binding sequence 5'-CATTAG-3' (Lee et al., 2008; Leonard et al., 1992) (Figure 1—figure supplement 3D).
evidence: The claim is supported by EMSA data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3D and citations to previous studies (Lee et al., 2008; Leonard et al., 1992) that identified the Isl1 binding sequence.

claim: The DF4-recognizing LIM transcription factors Lhx2 and Lhx3 do not bind the DF3 sequence.
source: Conversely, the DF4-recognizing LIM transcription factors Lhx2 and Lhx3 do not bind the DF3 sequence (Figure 1—figure supplement 3D).
evidence: The claim is supported by EMSA data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3D.

claim: Tgfb1i1 binds the α-enhancer indirectly, possibly via an interaction with LIM domain transcription factors.
source: Collectively, these results suggest Tgfb1i1 binds the α-enhancer indirectly, possibly via an interaction with these LIM domain transcription factors.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the collective EMSA and ChIP data showing Tgfb1i1 associates with the enhancer despite lacking DNA-binding motifs.

claim: Lhx3 is expressed in cone bipolar cells but not in amacrine cells.
source: Lhx3 is expressed in cone bipolar cells but not in amacrine cells, including the Pax6 α-GFP-positive subpopulation (Figure 1C; Figure 1—figure supplement 3A,B) (Balasubramanian et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 3A,B, and corroborated by citation to Balasubramanian et al., 2014.

claim: Lhx2 is expressed primarily in Müller glia but also in amacrine cells, including those with α-enhancer activity.
source: On the contrary, Lhx2 is expressed primarily in Müller glia (Balasubramanian et al., 2014) but also in amacrine cells, including those with α-enhancer activity (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3A,B and citation to Balasubramanian et al., 2014.

claim: Lhx9 is expressed in amacrine cells, about 60% of which show Pax6 α-enhancer activity.
source: Lhx9 is also expressed in amacrine cells (Balasubramanian et al., 2014), about 60% of which show Pax6 α-enhancer activity (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3A,B and citation to Balasubramanian et al., 2014.

claim: Both Lhx2 and Lhx9 activate the Pax6 α-luciferase reporter in a dose-dependent manner.
source: Both Lhx2 and Lhx9 activate the Pax6 α-luciferase reporter in a dose-dependent manner (Figure 2A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 2A and 2B.

claim: Lhx3 and Lhx4 do not affect α-enhancer activity alone.
source: In contrast, Lhx3 and Lhx4 do not affect α-enhancer activity alone (Figure 2A), but they antagonize Pax6-induced activation of the α-enhancer (Figure 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Lhx3 and Lhx4 antagonize Pax6-induced activation of the α-enhancer.
source: In contrast, Lhx3 and Lhx4 do not affect α-enhancer activity alone (Figure 2A), but they antagonize Pax6-induced activation of the α-enhancer (Figure 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Isl1 is expressed in ON bipolar cells and cholinergic amacrine cells.
source: Isl1 is expressed in ON bipolar cells and cholinergic amacrine cells (Elshatory et al., 2007; Galli-Resta et al., 1997; Haverkamp et al., 2003), but not in Pax6 α-enhancer-active amacrine cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Elshatory et al., 2007; Galli-Resta et al., 1997; Haverkamp et al., 2003) and immunostaining data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3A,B.

claim: Isl1 is not expressed in Pax6 α-enhancer-active amacrine cells.
source: Isl1 is expressed in ON bipolar cells and cholinergic amacrine cells (Elshatory et al., 2007; Galli-Resta et al., 1997; Haverkamp et al., 2003), but not in Pax6 α-enhancer-active amacrine cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3A,B.

claim: Isl1 does not affect Pax6 α-enhancer activity alone.
source: Isl1 does not affect Pax6 α-enhancer activity alone, but it does activate the enhancer in the presence of Pax6 (Figure 2A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Isl1 activates the Pax6 α-enhancer in the presence of Pax6.
source: Isl1 does not affect Pax6 α-enhancer activity alone, but it does activate the enhancer in the presence of Pax6 (Figure 2A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: LIM domain transcription factors in the mouse retina can be categorized as stimulatory (Lhx2 and Lhx9), inhibitory (Lhx3 and Lhx4), or context-sensitive (Isl1) based on their effects on Pax6 α-enhancer.
source: Together, these results suggest LIM domain transcription factors in the mouse retina can be categorized based on how they affect Pax6 α-enhancer—some are stimulatory (i.e., Lhx2 and Lhx9), some are inhibitory (i.e., Lhx3 and Lhx4), and some are context-sensitive (i.e., Isl1).
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the collective luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 2A and 2B.

claim: Tgfb1i1 inhibits Pax6-induced α-enhancer activity upon overexpression.
source: Tgfb1i1, although it is unable to bind the α-enhancer directly (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B), inhibits Pax6-induced α-enhancer activity upon overexpression (Figure 2C).
evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The inhibition of the α-enhancer by Tgfb1i1 is more significant when Tgfb1i1 is co-expressed with both Lhx3 and Isl1.
source: This inhibition of the α-enhancer is even more significant when Tgfb1i1 is co-expressed with both Lhx3 and Isl1 (Figure 2D,E).
evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 2D and 2E.

claim: Multiple LIM domains of Tgfb1i1 allow it to form a multi-protein complex that blocks α-enhancer-dependent gene expression.
source: We hypothesized that multiple LIM domains of Tgfb1i1 allow it to form a multi-protein complex that blocks α-enhancer-dependent gene expression.
evidence: The claim is a hypothesis based on the known structure of Tgfb1i1 and the observed inhibitory effects on the α-enhancer.

claim: Lmo4 prevents Isl1 and Lhx3 from interacting with one another or with other LIM domain-containing proteins.
source: To assess this, we co-expressed these LIM domain transcription factors with Lmo4 (LIM-domain-only 4), which prevents Isl1 and Lhx3 from interacting with one another or with other LIM domain-containing proteins (Thaler et al., 2002).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Thaler et al., 2002, which characterized the function of Lmo4.

claim: Lmo4 alone causes a dose-dependent increase in α-enhancer activity.
source: Lmo4 alone caused a dose-dependent increase in α-enhancer activity and potentiated Pax6-induced activation of the α-enhancer (Figure 2C).
evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Lmo4 potentiates Pax6-induced activation of the α-enhancer.
source: Lmo4 alone caused a dose-dependent increase in α-enhancer activity and potentiated Pax6-induced activation of the α-enhancer (Figure 2C).
evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: In the presence of Lmo4, Lhx3 and Isl1 cannot inhibit the α-enhancer.
source: In the presence of Lmo4, Lhx3 and Isl1 cannot inhibit the α-enhancer (Figure 2D).
evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Tgfb1i1 and Lmo4 oppositely regulate α-enhancer activity by antagonistically modulating the formation of the LIM domain transcription factor complex.
source: Thus, Tgfb1i1 and Lmo4 appear to oppositely regulate α-enhancer activity by antagonistically modulating the formation of the LIM domain transcription factor complex.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the collective luciferase reporter assay data showing opposite effects of Tgfb1i1 and Lmo4.

claim: Isl1 is detected in complexes recovered using Lhx3 and Tgfb1i1 from P7 mouse retina.
source: We were able to detect Isl1 in complexes recovered using Lhx3 and Tgfb1i1, which are also capable of precipitating one another (Figure 3A).
evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Lhx3 and Tgfb1i1 are capable of precipitating one another in P7 mouse retina.
source: We were able to detect Isl1 in complexes recovered using Lhx3 and Tgfb1i1, which are also capable of precipitating one another (Figure 3A).
evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Isl1, Lhx3, and Tgfb1i1 may exist as a complex in the retina.
source: This suggests these three proteins may exist as a complex in the retina.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the co-immunoprecipitation data showing mutual interactions among the three proteins.

claim: Isl1 binds to Lhx3 with its homeodomain (HD) and/or LIM binding domain (LBD).
source: In the co-immunoprecipitation experiments, we found that Isl1 binds to Lhx3 with its homeodomain (HD) and/or LIM binding domain (LBD), as reported previously (Thaler et al., 2002), whereas it interacts with Tgfb1i1 with its LIM domain(s) (Figure 3B [left column]; Figure 3—figure supplement 1B,C).
evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1B,C, and corroborated by citation to Thaler et al., 2002.

claim: Isl1 interacts with Tgfb1i1 with its LIM domain(s).
source: In the co-immunoprecipitation experiments, we found that Isl1 binds to Lhx3 with its homeodomain (HD) and/or LIM binding domain (LBD), as reported previously (Thaler et al., 2002), whereas it interacts with Tgfb1i1 with its LIM domain(s) (Figure 3B [left column]; Figure 3—figure supplement 1B,C).
evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1B,C.

claim: Lhx3 binds to Tgfb1i1 and Isl1 via its LIM domain(s).
source: Lhx3 binds to Tgfb1i1 and Isl1 via its LIM domain(s) (Figure 3B [center column]; Figure 3—figure supplement 1E,F).
evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1E,F.

claim: Tgfb1i1 uses LIM domain(s) to interact with Isl1 and Lhx3.
source: Tgfb1i1 also uses LIM domain(s) to interact with Isl1 and Lhx3 (Figure 3B [right columns]; Figure 3—figure supplement 1H,I).
evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1H,I.

claim: Overexpressed Tgfb1i1 enhances the association between Lhx3 and Isl1.
source: We found overexpressed Tgfb1i1 further enhanced the association between Lhx3 and Isl1 (Figure 3C).
evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Lmo4 induces a dose-dependent decrease in the association between Isl1 and Lhx3.
source: Lmo4, in contrast, induces a dose-dependent decrease in the association between Isl1 and Lhx3 (Figure 3D).
evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Tgfb1i1 links Isl1 and Lhx3 to form a hetero-tetrameric (or larger) complex while Lmo4 interferes with the complex formation.
source: Collectively, these results suggest Tgfb1i1 links Isl1 and Lhx3 to form a hetero-tetrameric (or larger) complex while Lmo4 interferes with the complex formation.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the collective co-immunoprecipitation data showing Tgfb1i1 enhances and Lmo4 reduces Isl1-Lhx3 association.

claim: Pax6 interacts with various homeodomain-containing proteins.
source: It is possible Pax6 interacts with the homeodomains of Isl1 and Lhx3 to form a Pax6-LIM protein complex, since Pax6 reportedly interacts with various homeodomain-containing proteins (Granger et al., 2006; Mikkola et al., 2001).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Granger et al., 2006; Mikkola et al., 2001) that demonstrated Pax6 interactions with homeodomain proteins.

claim: Pax6 interacts only with Isl1, but not Lhx3, via its paired domain (PD).
source: We also found Pax6 interacts only with Isl1, but not Lhx3, via its paired domain (PD) (Figure 3E; Figure 3—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 3E and Figure 3—figure supplement 1G.

claim: Both the HD and LIM domains of Isl1 participate in interaction with Pax6.
source: Both the HD and LIM domains of Isl1 participated to interact with Pax6, thus Pax6 might compete with Tgfb1i1 and Lhx3 to bind Isl1 (Figure 3H, top; Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 3H and Figure 3—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Pax6 might compete with Tgfb1i1 and Lhx3 to bind Isl1.
source: Both the HD and LIM domains of Isl1 participated to interact with Pax6, thus Pax6 might compete with Tgfb1i1 and Lhx3 to bind Isl1 (Figure 3H, top; Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the observation that Pax6 and Tgfb1i1/Lhx3 bind overlapping domains of Isl1.

claim: Isl1, Lhx3, and Tgfb1i1 reduce the binding of Pax6 to the α-enhancer when all three are co-expressed.
source: Using ChIP analyses in the cultured cells, we found Isl1, Lhx3, and Tgfb1i1 reduce the binding of Pax6 to the α-enhancer when all three are co-expressed but not when expressed individually (Figure 3G, three right graphs).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP data shown in Figure 3G.

claim: Pax6 expression interferes with the access of Tgfb1i1 to the α-enhancer.
source: Conversely, Pax6 expression interferes with the access of Tgfb1i1 to the α-enhancer (Figure 3G, rightmost graph).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP data shown in Figure 3G.

claim: Pax6 does not affect Lhx3 binding to the α-enhancer.
source: Pax6 does not affect Lhx3 binding to the α-enhancer, but it promotes Isl1 binding (Figure 3H, two center graphs).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP data shown in Figure 3H.

claim: Pax6 promotes Isl1 binding to the α-enhancer.
source: Pax6 does not affect Lhx3 binding to the α-enhancer, but it promotes Isl1 binding (Figure 3H, two center graphs).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP data shown in Figure 3H.

claim: Two different transcription factor complexes occupy the α-enhancer region: the Isl1-Pax6 complex that activates the α-enhancer, and the Isl1-Tgfb1i1-Lhx3 complex that inhibits Pax6 access.
source: Together, these molecular interaction results suggest two different transcription factor complexes occupying the α-enhancer region. The Isl1-Pax6 complex binds to the DF3 and PBS and activates the α-enhancer (Figure 3H, top), whereas the Isl1-Tgfb1i1-Lhx3 complex binds to DF3 and DF4 to cover the area between those two sequences and inhibit the access of Pax6 to DF3 (Figure 3H, bottom).
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the collective ChIP and co-immunoprecipitation data, summarized in Figure 3H.

claim: Tgfb1i1−/− mouse retinas show more cells positive for the Pax6 α-GFP reporter than the retinas of their Tgfb1i1+/+ littermates.
source: In support of the idea that Tgfb1i1 plays an important role in the inhibition of Pax6 α-enhancer, the Tgfb1i1−/− mouse retinas show more cells positive for the Pax6 α-GFP reporter than the retinas of their Tgfb1i1+/+ littermates (Figure 4A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining and quantification data shown in Figure 4A and 4B.

claim: Tgfb1i1−/− mouse retinas have more Pax6-positive amacrine cells than Tgfb1i1+/+ littermates.
source: Tgfb1i1−/− mouse retinas have more Pax6-positive amacrine cells and fewer Vsx2-positive bipolar cells than Tgfb1i1+/+ littermates (Figure 4C–F).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining and quantification data shown in Figure 4C-F.

claim: Tgfb1i1−/− mouse retinas have fewer Vsx2-positive bipolar cells than Tgfb1i1+/+ littermates.
source: Tgfb1i1−/− mouse retinas have more Pax6-positive amacrine cells and fewer Vsx2-positive bipolar cells than Tgfb1i1+/+ littermates (Figure 4C–F).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining and quantification data shown in Figure 4C-F.

claim: Among amacrine cell subtypes, only GABAergic amacrine cells show a significant increase in Tgfb1i1−/− retinas.
source: Among those amacrine cell subtypes, only GABAergic amacrine cells showed a significant increase, while the numbers of cholinergic and glycinergic amacrine cells remain unchanged (Figure 4C,D).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining and quantification data shown in Figure 4C and 4D.

claim: The numbers of cholinergic and glycinergic amacrine cells remain unchanged in Tgfb1i1−/− retinas.
source: Among those amacrine cell subtypes, only GABAergic amacrine cells showed a significant increase, while the numbers of cholinergic and glycinergic amacrine cells remain unchanged (Figure 4C,D).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining and quantification data shown in Figure 4C and 4D.

claim: The Pax6 α-GFP-positive cells are mainly GABAergic amacrine cells.
source: Moreover, the Pax6 α-GFP-positive cells are mainly GABAergic amacrine cells (Figure 4C,D; Figure 4—figure supplement 1), suggesting a positive relationship between Pax6 α-enhancer activity and GABAergic amacrine cell fate and a negative role of Tgfb1i1 in this.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 4C, 4D, and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: There is a positive relationship between Pax6 α-enhancer activity and GABAergic amacrine cell fate.
source: Moreover, the Pax6 α-GFP-positive cells are mainly GABAergic amacrine cells (Figure 4C,D; Figure 4—figure supplement 1), suggesting a positive relationship between Pax6 α-enhancer activity and GABAergic amacrine cell fate and a negative role of Tgfb1i1 in this.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the observation that Pax6 α-GFP-positive cells are predominantly GABAergic.

claim: Tgfb1i1 plays a negative role in GABAergic amacrine cell fate.
source: Moreover, the Pax6 α-GFP-positive cells are mainly GABAergic amacrine cells (Figure 4C,D; Figure 4—figure supplement 1), suggesting a positive relationship between Pax6 α-enhancer activity and GABAergic amacrine cell fate and a negative role of Tgfb1i1 in this.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the increase in GABAergic amacrine cells in Tgfb1i1−/− retinas.

claim: The Tgfb1i1−/− mouse retinas show fewer Vsx1-positive OFF bipolar cells without significant changes in G0α-positive ON bipolar cells.
source: Among bipolar cell subtypes, the Tgfb1i1−/− mouse retinas show fewer Vsx1-positive OFF bipolar cells without significant changes in G0α-positive ON bipolar cells, including PKCα-positive rod bipolar cells (Figure 4E,F).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining and quantification data shown in Figure 4E and 4F.

claim: The numbers of type-2 OFF bipolar cells, which are positive to Bhlhb5 and Recoverin, are not greatly different between Tgfb1i1+/+ and Tgfb1i1−/− mouse retinas.
source: However, the numbers of type-2 OFF bipolar cells, which are positive to Bhlhb5 and Recoverin, are not greatly different between Tgfb1i1+/+ and Tgfb1i1−/− mouse retinas (Figure 4C–F; Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining and quantification data shown in Figure 4C-F and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Tgfb1i1 is necessary for the development of Vsx1-positive OFF bipolar cells, except for type-2 subset, in mouse retina.
source: The results therefore suggest that Tgfb1i1 is necessary for the development of Vsx1-positive OFF bipolar cells, except for type-2 subset, in mouse retina.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the selective reduction of Vsx1-positive OFF bipolar cells (excluding type-2) in Tgfb1i1−/− retinas.

claim: GABAergic amacrine cell identities of retinal cells expressing Cas9 and Lhx3 sgRNA were significantly enhanced.
source: We found GABAergic amacrine cell identities of the retinal cells expressing the constructs were significantly enhanced, whereas OFF bipolar cell identities of the cells were remarkably diminished (Figure 4—figure supplement 2B–D).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining and quantification data from CRISPR/Cas9-mediated Lhx3 deletion experiments shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2B-D.

claim: OFF bipolar cell identities of retinal cells expressing Cas9 and Lhx3 sgRNA were remarkably diminished.
source: We found GABAergic amacrine cell identities of the retinal cells expressing the constructs were significantly enhanced, whereas OFF bipolar cell identities of the cells were remarkably diminished (Figure 4—figure supplement 2B–D).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining and quantification data from CRISPR/Cas9-mediated Lhx3 deletion experiments shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2B-D.

claim: Tgfb1i1 supports the development of OFF bipolar cell subsets while it antagonizes the development of GABAergic amacrine cell subset by forming Lhx3-containing protein complex that inhibits Pax6 α-enhancer activity in post-natal mouse retina.
source: Collectively, our results suggest that Tgfb1i1 supports the development of OFF bipolar cell subsets, while it antagonizes the development of GABAergic amacrine cell subset, by forming Lhx3-containing protein complex that inhibits Pax6 α-enhancer activity in post-natal mouse retina.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the collective data from Tgfb1i1−/− and Lhx3 deletion experiments.

claim: In P14 mouse retinas, Lhx3-positive bipolar cells co-expressing Isl1 comprise only 20% of total Lhx3-positive cells.
source: In P14 mouse retinas, Lhx3-positive bipolar cells co-expressing Isl1 comprise only 20% of total Lhx3-positive cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B,C).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining and quantification data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B and 1C.

claim: 82% of Lhx3-positive retinal cells co-express Isl1 at P7.
source: In contrast, 82% of Lhx3-positive retinal cells co-express Isl1 at P7, which is when Tgfb1i1 is expressed in most retinal cell types apart from amacrine cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A,C).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining and quantification data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A and 1C.

claim: The Isl1-Tgfb1i1-Lhx3 complex may form in the retinal cells around the first post-natal week at the peak of bipolar cell development.
source: This suggests the Isl1-Tgfb1i1-Lhx3 complex may form in the retinal cells around the first post-natal week at the peak of bipolar cell development (Morrow et al., 2008; Rapaport et al., 2004).
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the temporal expression patterns of the proteins, supported by citations to studies on bipolar cell development (Morrow et al., 2008; Rapaport et al., 2004).

claim: The interaction between Isl1 and Lhx3 is significantly reduced in P7 Tgfb1i1−/− retinas.
source: Supporting this, the interaction between Isl1 and Lhx3 is significantly reduced in P7 Tgfb1i1−/− retinas (Figure 5A, top).
evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Reduced Isl1-Lhx3 interaction might trigger an over-activation of Pax6 transcription driven by the α-enhancer.
source: This might trigger an over-activation of Pax6 transcription, driven by the α-enhancer.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the reduced Isl1-Lhx3 interaction in Tgfb1i1−/− retinas.

claim: Pax6 levels did not differ in Tgfb1i1−/− and Tgfb1i1+/+ mouse retinas.
source: However, Pax6 levels did not differ in Tgfb1i1−/− and Tgfb1i1+/+ mouse retinas (Figure 5B, larger Pax6 bands), despite the increase of Pax6-positive cells in Tgfb1i1−/− mouse retina (Figure 4C,D).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: A specific increase in the level of Pax6ΔPD isoform was observed in the Tgfb1i1−/− mouse retina.
source: We did, instead, observe a specific increase in the level of Pax6ΔPD isoform, which is an alternative transcript produced at downstream of the α-enhancer sequence (Lakowski et al., 2007; Plaza et al., 1995), in the Tgfb1i1−/− mouse retina (Figure 5B, smaller Pax6 bands).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 5B and citations to previous studies (Lakowski et al., 2007; Plaza et al., 1995) characterizing the Pax6ΔPD isoform.

claim: Pax6ΔPD isoform is selectively enriched in Pax6 α-GFP-positive cells purified from P7 P6α-CreiGFP retinas by FACS.
source: This Pax6ΔPD isoform is selectively enriched in Pax6 α-GFP-positive cells purified from P7 P6α-CreiGFP retinas by fluorescence activated cell sorting (FACS) (Figure 5C).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blot data from FACS-purified cells shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Hyperactivation of the Pax6 α-enhancer in Tgfb1i1−/− retinas triggers ectopic expression of Pax6ΔPD isoform, but not the canonical Pax6.
source: Our results, thus, suggest hyperactivation of the Pax6 α-enhancer in Tgfb1i1−/− retinas triggers ectopic expression of Pax6ΔPD isoform, but not the canonical Pax6.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the selective increase in Pax6ΔPD but not full-length Pax6 in Tgfb1i1−/− retinas.

claim: About 54% of EGFP-positive INL cells in P14 mouse retinas electroporated with pCAGIG-Pax6ΔPD DNA at P0 are identified as Syntaxin-positive amacrine cells.
source: About 54% of EGFP-positive INL cells in P14 mouse retinas, which were electroporated with the pCAGIG-Pax6ΔPD DNA at P0, are identified as Syntaxin-positive amacrine cells, whereas only 26% of EGFP-positive INL cells are amacrine cells in the retinas electroporated with control pCAGIG DNA (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A [top row], D).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining and quantification data from electroporation experiments shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2A and 2D.

claim: About 85% of EGFP-positive INL cells in P14 mouse retinas electroporated with pCAGIG-Pax6 DNA at P0 are identified as amacrine cells.
source: This is also contrary to the results of pCAGIG-Pax6-electroporated mouse retinas, in which about 85% of EGFP-positive INL cells are identified as amacrine cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A [top row, middle], D).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining and quantification data from electroporation experiments shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2A and 2D.

claim: Majority of EGFP-positive amacrine cells in the pCAGIG-Pax6ΔPD-electroporated retinas are predicted as GABAergic amacrine cells.
source: Moreover, by showing insignificantly different marker positivity with EGFP;Syntaxin double-positive INL cells (54% ± 7.56%(Syntaxin) vs. 46% ± 7.33%(Gad67)), majority of EGFP-positive amacrine cells in the pCAGIG-Pax6ΔPD-electroporated retinas are predicted as GABAergic amacrine cells, which are approximately half of the EGFP;Syntaxin double-positive amacrine cell population in pCAGIG-Pax6-electroporated mouse retinas (85% ± 7.2%(Syntaxin) vs. 44% ± 9.17%(Gad67)) (Figure 5F,G; Figure 5—figure supplement 2A [second row], D).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining and quantification data from electroporation experiments shown in Figure 5F, 5G, and Figure 5—figure supplement 2A and 2D.

claim: Pax6ΔPD preferentially supports GABAergic amacrine cell fate.
source: Together, these results suggest that Pax6ΔPD preferentially supports GABAergic amacrine cell fate, while full-length Pax6 induces all amacrine cell types in a similar ratio observed in the normal mouse retina (Voinescu et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the electroporation data showing preferential GABAergic fate in Pax6ΔPD-expressing cells, with citation to Voinescu et al., 2009 for normal amacrine cell ratios.

claim: Full-length Pax6 induces all amacrine cell types in a similar ratio observed in the normal mouse retina.
source: Together, these results suggest that Pax6ΔPD preferentially supports GABAergic amacrine cell fate, while full-length Pax6 induces all amacrine cell types in a similar ratio observed in the normal mouse retina (Voinescu et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the electroporation data, with citation to Voinescu et al., 2009 for normal amacrine cell ratios.

claim: Mouse retinas expressing ectopic Pax6ΔPD show almost no EGFP-positive cells co-expressing OFF bipolar cell markers including Vsx1, Recoverin, and Bhlhb5.
source: Mouse retinas expressing ectopic Pax6ΔPD show almost no EGFP-positive cells co-expressing OFF bipolar cell markers including Vsx1, Recoverin, and Bhlhb5 (Figure 5F [bottom row], G; Figure 5—figure supplement 2B,D).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining and quantification data from electroporation experiments shown in Figure 5F, 5G, and Figure 5—figure supplement 2B and 2D.

claim: Significant numbers of EGFP-positive cells co-expressed ON bipolar cell marker G0α in pCAGIG-Pax6ΔPD-electroporated mouse retinas.
source: On the contrary, significant numbers of EGFP-positive cells co-expressed ON bipolar cell marker G0α in pCAGIG-Pax6ΔPD-electroporated mouse retinas, and the numbers are not significantly different from those in pCAGIG-electroporated samples (Figure 5—figure supplement 2B,D).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining and quantification data from electroporation experiments shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2B and 2D.

claim: EGFP-positive cells in pCAGIG-Pax6-electroporated mouse retinas are almost absent of both ON and OFF bipolar cell marker co-expression.
source: EGFP-positive cells in pCAGIG-Pax6-electroporated mouse retinas, however, are almost absent of both ON and OFF bipolar cell marker co-expression (Figure 5—figure supplement 2B,D).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining and quantification data from electroporation experiments shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2B and 2D.

claim: Pax6ΔPD inhibits only OFF bipolar cell fate.
source: The results therefore suggest that Pax6ΔPD inhibits only OFF bipolar cell fate, while full-length Pax6 suppress both ON and OFF bipolar cell fates.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the electroporation data showing selective loss of OFF bipolar markers in Pax6ΔPD-expressing cells.

claim: Full-length Pax6 suppresses both ON and OFF bipolar cell fates.
source: The results therefore suggest that Pax6ΔPD inhibits only OFF bipolar cell fate, while full-length Pax6 suppress both ON and OFF bipolar cell fates.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the electroporation data showing loss of both ON and OFF bipolar markers in Pax6-expressing cells.

claim: The gross morphologies of Pax6ΔPBS/ΔPBS mouse eyes are indistinguishable from Pax6+/+ WT eyes.
source: Despite the Pax6 α-enhancer being active in the mouse retina from embryo to adult, the gross morphologies of Pax6ΔPBS/ΔPBS mouse eyes are indistinguishable from Pax6+/+ WT eyes (Figure 6B), implicating dispensable roles of Pax6 α-enhancer-induced Pax6ΔPD expression in the eye and retinal development.
evidence: The claim is supported by eye morphology images shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Pax6 α-enhancer-induced Pax6ΔPD expression plays dispensable roles in the eye and retinal development.
source: Despite the Pax6 α-enhancer being active in the mouse retina from embryo to adult, the gross morphologies of Pax6ΔPBS/ΔPBS mouse eyes are indistinguishable from Pax6+/+ WT eyes (Figure 6B), implicating dispensable roles of Pax6 α-enhancer-induced Pax6ΔPD expression in the eye and retinal development.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the normal eye morphology in Pax6ΔPBS/ΔPBS mice.

claim: In P14 Pax6ΔPBS/ΔPBS retinas, the α-enhancer-driven GFP and Pax6ΔPD expression are reduced significantly, but not entirely abolished.
source: However, in P14 Pax6ΔPBS/ΔPBS retinas, the α-enhancer-driven GFP and Pax6ΔPD expression are reduced significantly, but not entirely abolished (Figure 6B–D).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining and Western blot data shown in Figure 6B-D.

claim: There is presence of positive regulator(s) of the α-enhancer in the mouse retina other than Pax6.
source: Since Pax6 does not bind and activate the Pax6ΔPBS α-enhancer (Figure 6—figure supplement 1), this suggests the presence of positive regulator(s) of the α-enhancer in the mouse retina other than Pax6.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the residual α-enhancer activity in Pax6ΔPBS/ΔPBS retinas, supported by data in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: P14 Pax6ΔPBS/ΔPBS retinas show significantly fewer GABAergic amacrine cells than the retinas of Pax6+/+ WT littermates.
source: P14 Pax6ΔPBS/ΔPBS retinas show significantly fewer GABAergic amacrine cells than the retinas of Pax6+/+ WT littermates, despite similar total numbers of Pax6-positive amacrine cells (Figure 6E [left two columns], F; Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining and quantification data shown in Figure 6E, 6F, and Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: Pax6ΔPBS/ΔPBS retinas show more OFF bipolar cells (i.e., Vsx1-positive), despite similar total numbers of Vsx2-positive bipolar cells.
source: Conversely, Pax6ΔPBS/ΔPBS retinas show more OFF bipolar cells (i.e., Vsx1-positive), despite similar total numbers of Vsx2-positive bipolar cells (Figure 6E [right two columns], F; Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining and quantification data shown in Figure 6E, 6F, and Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: The numbers of GABAergic amacrine cells were not significantly different between Pax6+/+ and Pax6ΔPBS/ΔPBS retinas until P4.
source: However, the numbers of GABAergic amacrine cells, which start to develop in the embryonic retina (Voinescu et al., 2009), were not significantly different between Pax6+/+ and Pax6ΔPBS/ΔPBS retinas until P4 when the bipolar cells start to develop (Figure 6—figure supplement 3A [bottom three rows], B).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining and quantification data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 3A and 3B, with citation to Voinescu et al., 2009 for GABAergic amacrine cell development timing.

claim: Pax6-dependent activation of Pax6 α-enhancer is not essential for the embryonic development of GABAergic amacrine cells.
source: The results therefore suggest that Pax6-dependent activation of Pax6 α-enhancer is not essential for the embryonic development of GABAergic amacrine cells but it might be necessary for the development and/or maintenance of those cells in the post-natal retina.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the normal GABAergic amacrine cell numbers in embryonic and early postnatal Pax6ΔPBS/ΔPBS retinas.

claim: Pax6-dependent activation of Pax6 α-enhancer might be necessary for the development and/or maintenance of GABAergic amacrine cells in the post-natal retina.
source: The results therefore suggest that Pax6-dependent activation of Pax6 α-enhancer is not essential for the embryonic development of GABAergic amacrine cells but it might be necessary for the development and/or maintenance of those cells in the post-natal retina.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the reduced GABAergic amacrine cells in postnatal Pax6ΔPBS/ΔPBS retinas.

claim: No BrdU;Bhlhb5 double-positive GABAergic amacrine cells were found in P14 WT, Tgfb1i1−/−, and Pax6ΔPBS/ΔPBS mouse retinas labeled between P4 and P7.
source: We failed to find BrdU;Bhlhb5 double-positive GABAergic amacrine cells in P14 WT, Tgfb1i1−/−, and Pax6ΔPBS/ΔPBS mouse retinas, suggesting the lack of newborn GABAergic amacrine cells in the post-natal mouse retinas (Figure 6—figure supplement 3C,E).
evidence: The claim is supported by BrdU labeling data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 3C and 3E.

claim: There is a lack of newborn GABAergic amacrine cells in the post-natal mouse retinas.
source: We failed to find BrdU;Bhlhb5 double-positive GABAergic amacrine cells in P14 WT, Tgfb1i1−/−, and Pax6ΔPBS/ΔPBS mouse retinas, suggesting the lack of newborn GABAergic amacrine cells in the post-natal mouse retinas (Figure 6—figure supplement 3C,E).
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the absence of BrdU-labeled GABAergic amacrine cells born postnatally.

claim: The number of BrdU;Vsx1 double-positive OFF bipolar cells in WT, Tgfb1i1−/−, and Pax6ΔPBS/ΔPBS mouse retinas were not significantly different from each other.
source: Furthermore, the number of BrdU;Vsx1 double-positive OFF bipolar cells in those mouse retinas were not significantly different each other (Figure 6—figure supplement 3C [bottom row], D), despite the remarkable decrease and increase of total Vsx1-positive cell numbers in P14 Tgfb1i1−/− and Pax6ΔPBS/ΔPBS in mouse retinas, respectively (Figure 4E,F; Figure 6E,F).
evidence: The claim is supported by BrdU labeling data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 3C and 3D.

claim: The alteration of OFF bipolar cells in Tgfb1i1−/− and Pax6ΔPBS/ΔPBS mutant mouse retinas was not caused by neurogenic fate changes of newborn retinal cells but may have resulted from fate change of preexisting retinal cells.
source: The results therefore suggest that the alteration of OFF bipolar cells in those two mutant mouse retinas was not caused by neurogenic fate changes of newborn retinal cells but may have resulted from fate change of preexisting retinal cells.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the unchanged numbers of newly born OFF bipolar cells despite changes in total OFF bipolar cell numbers.

claim: The numbers of Bhlhb5;BrdU-labeled GABAergic amacrine cells are significantly decreased in P7 Pax6ΔPBS/ΔPBS mouse retinas compared to WT littermate mouse retinas.
source: The numbers of Bhlhb5;BrdU-labeled GABAergic amacrine cells are significantly decreased in P7 Pax6ΔPBS/ΔPBS mouse retinas in comparison to their WT littermate mouse retinas (Figure 6—figure supplement 3D [top row], F).
evidence: The claim is supported by BrdU labeling data from E15 injection shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 3D and 3F.

claim: Vsx1;BrdU-labeled OFF bipolar cell numbers are significantly increased in the Pax6ΔPBS/ΔPBS mouse retinas.
source: Conversely, Vsx1;BrdU-labeled OFF bipolar cell numbers are significantly increased in the Pax6ΔPBS/ΔPBS mouse retinas (Figure 6—figure supplement 3D [bottom row], F).
evidence: The claim is supported by BrdU labeling data from E15 injection shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 3D and 3F.

claim: Pax6 and the Isl1-Tgfb1i1-Lhx3 complex in the post-natal mouse retina competitively regulate the Pax6 α-enhancer-driven expression of Pax6ΔPD, which maintains GABAergic amacrine cell fate against the transdifferentiation into OFF bipolar cells.
source: Taken together, these results suggest Pax6 and the Isl1-Tgfb1i1-Lhx3 complex in the post-natal mouse retina competitively regulate the Pax6 α-enhancer-driven expression of Pax6ΔPD, which maintains GABAergic amacrine cell fate against the transdifferentiation into OFF bipolar cells.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the collective BrdU labeling data showing fate changes of embryonically-born cells.

claim: There is a significant reduction in visual acuity of P60 Tgfb1i1−/− mice compared to age-matched WT and Pax6ΔPBS/ΔPBS mice.
source: Using the OptoMotry system (Prusky et al., 2004), we observed a significant reduction in visual acuity of P60 Tgfb1i1−/− mice compared to age-matched WT and Pax6ΔPBS/ΔPBS mice (Figure 7A, graph).
evidence: The claim is supported by visual acuity test data shown in Figure 7A, with citation to Prusky et al., 2004 for the OptoMotry system.

claim: The amplitudes for the a- and b-waves in dark-adapted (scotopic) and light-adapted (photopic) ERG responses of P60 Tgfb1i1−/− and Pax6ΔPBS/ΔPBS mouse eyes were unaltered in comparison to those of WT littermate controls.
source: Upon the measurement of light response of a whole retina by electroretinogram (ERG), the amplitudes for the a- and b-waves in dark-adapted (scotopic) and light-adapted (photopic) ERG responses of P60 Tgfb1i1−/− and Pax6ΔPBS/ΔPBS mouse eyes were, however, unaltered in comparison to those of WT littermate controls (Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by ERG data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: The functions of photoreceptors (determined by ERG a-waves) and ON bipolar cells (determined by ERG b-waves) are intact in Tgfb1i1−/− and Pax6ΔPBS/ΔPBS mutant mice.
source: The results suggest that the functions of photoreceptors (determined by ERG a-waves) and ON bipolar cells (determined by ERG b-waves) are intact in those mutant mice.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the normal ERG a-wave and b-wave amplitudes in the mutant mice.

claim: The numbers of photoreceptors and ON bipolar cells in P60 Tgfb1i1−/− and Pax6ΔPBS/ΔPBS mouse retinas were not significantly different from those in their littermate WT mice.
source: In support of this, the numbers of photoreceptors and ON bipolar cells in P60 Tgfb1i1−/− and Pax6ΔPBS/ΔPBS mouse retinas were not significantly different from those in their littermate WT mice (Figure 7—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining and quantification data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 2.

claim: The reduced visual acuity of Tgfb1i1−/− mice might be caused by either the changes of visual pathway components in the brain or the alterations of amacrine cells and RGCs at downstream of bipolar cells.
source: Therefore, the reduced visual acuity of Tgfb1i1−/− mice might be caused by either the changes of visual pathway components in the brain or the alterations of amacrine cells and RGCs at downstream of bipolar cells.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the normal photoreceptor and bipolar cell function but reduced visual acuity.

claim: There is an increase in the basal firing rate and mean spike number for the light-ON responses of P60 Tgfb1i1−/− retinas when compared to WT littermate controls.
source: We found an increase in the basal firing rate and mean spike number, but no change in maximum spike rate for the light-ON responses of P60 Tgfb1i1−/− retinas when compared to WT littermate controls (Figure 7B [top], C).
evidence: The claim is supported by MEA recording data shown in Figure 7B and 7C.

claim: There is no change in maximum spike rate for the light-ON responses of P60 Tgfb1i1−/− retinas when compared to WT littermate controls.
source: We found an increase in the basal firing rate and mean spike number, but no change in maximum spike rate for the light-ON responses of P60 Tgfb1i1−/− retinas when compared to WT littermate controls (Figure 7B [top], C).
evidence: The claim is supported by MEA recording data shown in Figure 7B and 7C.

claim: There is a reduction in the basal firing rate, maximum spike rate, and mean spike number for the ON responses of P60 Pax6ΔPBS/ΔPBS retinas.
source: Conversely, we observed a reduction in the basal firing rate, maximum spike rate, and mean spike number for the ON responses of P60 Pax6ΔPBS/ΔPBS retinas (Figure 7B [bottom], D).
evidence: The claim is supported by MEA recording data shown in Figure 7B and 7D.

claim: A significant number of RGCs in P60 Tgfb1i1−/− retinas do not return to the resting state after a transient light response.
source: Interestingly, a significant number of RGCs in P60 Tgfb1i1−/− retinas do not return to the resting state after a transient light response (Figure 7B, arrowhead).
evidence: The claim is supported by MEA recording data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: P6α amacrine cells might disinhibit ON response by acting to other inhibitory retinal neurons in light-ON pathway.
source: Considering the GABAergic identity of P6α amacrine cells and the increase of the cells in the Tgfb1i1−/− retinas (Figure 4C,D; Figure 4—figure supplement 1), it suggests this specific amacrine cell subset might disinhibit ON response by acting to other inhibitory retinal neurons in light-ON pathway (Chávez et al., 2010; Demb and Singer, 2012; Eggers et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the GABAergic identity of P6α amacrine cells and the sustained light response in Tgfb1i1−/− retinas, supported by citations to previous studies (Chávez et al., 2010; Demb and Singer, 2012; Eggers et al., 2013) on disinhibition mechanisms.

claim: Tgfb1i1−/− mice learn the visual detection task faster than WT mice.
source: Tgfb1i1−/− mice not only learn this task faster than WT mice (Figure 7—figure supplement 3B), but they also show more sensitive detection of the light stimuli (Figure 7E).
evidence: The claim is supported by behavioral test data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 3B.

claim: Tgfb1i1−/− mice show more sensitive detection of light stimuli than WT mice.
source: Tgfb1i1−/− mice not only learn this task faster than WT mice (Figure 7—figure supplement 3B), but they also show more sensitive detection of the light stimuli (Figure 7E).
evidence: The claim is supported by behavioral test data shown in Figure 7E.

claim: Tgfb1i1−/− mice perform worse than WT mice in a visual task requiring detection of a drifting grate stimulus after a light stimulus.
source: However, in a second visual task requiring mice to detect a drifting grate stimulus after a light stimulus, Tgfb1i1−/− mice perform worse than WT mice (Figure 7F; Figure 7—figure supplement 3C,D).
evidence: The claim is supported by behavioral test data shown in Figure 7F and Figure 7—figure supplement 3C and 3D.

claim: Tgfb1i1−/− retinas are more slowly re-sensitized after light exposure than WT retinas.
source: This suggests Tgfb1i1−/− retinas are more slowly re-sensitized after light exposure than WT retinas.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the poor performance of Tgfb1i1−/− mice in the visual adaptation task.

claim: The re-sensitization of Pax6ΔPBS/ΔPBS retinas is significantly faster than WT retinas.
source: Conversely, the re-sensitization of Pax6ΔPBS/ΔPBS retinas is significantly faster than WT retinas, despite being less sensitive to light (Figure 7F,G; Figure 7—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by behavioral test data shown in Figure 7F, 7G, and Figure 7—figure supplement 3.

claim: Pax6ΔPBS/ΔPBS retinas are less sensitive to light than WT retinas.
source: Conversely, the re-sensitization of Pax6ΔPBS/ΔPBS retinas is significantly faster than WT retinas, despite being less sensitive to light (Figure 7F,G; Figure 7—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the behavioral test data.

claim: P6α amacrine cells control the tone of light-ON retinal pathway.
source: Collectively, the results suggest that P6α amacrine cells control the tone of light-ON retinal pathway.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the collective MEA and behavioral data showing opposite effects in Tgfb1i1−/− and Pax6ΔPBS/ΔPBS mice.

claim: The overall tone of light-ON pathway was increased in Tgfb1i1−/− mouse retinas, which have extra P6α amacrine cells.
source: The overall tone of light-ON pathway was increased in Tgfb1i1−/− mouse retinas, which have extra P6α amacrine cells, whereas it is decreased in Pax6ΔPBS/ΔPBS mouse retinas having reduced P6α amacrine cell number.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the MEA and behavioral data.

claim: The overall tone of light-ON pathway is decreased in Pax6ΔPBS/ΔPBS mouse retinas having reduced P6α amacrine cell number.
source: The overall tone of light-ON pathway was increased in Tgfb1i1−/− mouse retinas, which have extra P6α amacrine cells, whereas it is decreased in Pax6ΔPBS/ΔPBS mouse retinas having reduced P6α amacrine cell number.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the MEA and behavioral data.

claim: The light-ON pathway is augmented in Tgfb1i1−/− mouse retinas and attenuated in Pax6ΔPBS/ΔPBS mouse retinas to make the retinas hypersensitive and hyposensitive to light stimulus, respectively.
source: Consequently, the light-ON pathway is augmented in Tgfb1i1−/− mouse retinas and attenuated in Pax6ΔPBS/ΔPBS mouse retinas to make the retinas hypersensitive and hyposensitive to light stimulus, respectively (Figure 7B–E).
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the collective MEA and behavioral data shown in Figure 7B-E.

claim: The Tgfb1i1−/− mouse retinas cannot be re-sensitized as fast as WT retinas.
source: On the other hand, the Tgfb1i1−/− mouse retinas cannot be re-sensitized as fast as WT retinas, while the Pax6ΔPBS/ΔPBS mouse retinas can be re-sensitized more quickly than WT retinas after a light stimulus.
evidence: The claim is supported by behavioral test data.

claim: The Pax6ΔPBS/ΔPBS mouse retinas can be re-sensitized more quickly than WT retinas after a light stimulus.
source: On the other hand, the Tgfb1i1−/− mouse retinas cannot be re-sensitized as fast as WT retinas, while the Pax6ΔPBS/ΔPBS mouse retinas can be re-sensitized more quickly than WT retinas after a light stimulus.
evidence: The claim is supported by behavioral test data.

claim: The P6α amacrine cells may inhibit the activity of post-synaptic partners, which can be predicted as an inhibitory neuron in light-ON pathway.
source: Given the GABAergic identity of the cells, the P6α amacrine cells may inhibit the activity of post-synaptic partners, which are not identified yet but can be predicted as an inhibitory neuron in light-ON pathway (Figure 7F).
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the GABAergic identity of P6α amacrine cells and the visual adaptation data.

claim: The proper number of P6α amacrine cells should be present in the retina to respond to light efficiently and adequately.
source: Therefore, the results indicate that the proper number of P6α amacrine cells should be present in the retina to respond to light efficiently and adequately.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the collective visual function data from mice with altered P6α amacrine cell numbers.
